tagline: The viral hidden-word bluffing game vs a party game where everyone talks.
metaTitle: Imposter Game vs Tadado: Which Party Game Wins Game Night?
metaDescription: Love the Imposter word game? See how it compares with Tadado's Forbidden Words and Heads Up modes: one phone, no ads, AI decks and a free starter deck.
hook: Imposter is all about suspicion. Tadado is all about shouting the answer before the timer runs out. Here is when each one makes the night.
about: Imposter (also called Who's the Spy or the impostor word game) went viral because it needs almost nothing: one phone is passed around, everyone secretly sees the same word except one player, and the group gives one-word hints until someone gets voted out as the impostor.

It is a bluffing game first. The fun comes from reading faces, defending yourself and the big reveal at the end of a round. That makes it brilliant for groups who love debate, and quieter for players who would rather be guessing and laughing every few seconds.
pickThem: Your group loves bluffing, accusing and dramatic reveals
You want a slow-burn round with lots of discussion
Everyone is happy to sit and talk rather than race a timer
pickTadado: You want nonstop laughing with a new word every few seconds
Some friends are shy and prefer guessing to lying
You want two modes, Forbidden Words and Heads Up, in one app

rows.feature: Works with one phone passed around

steps: Download Tadado and open the free Tadado Mix deck.
Pick Forbidden Words for teams or Heads Up for forehead guessing.
Want the Imposter vibe of inside jokes? Type your group's topic into the AI deck builder.

faq.q: Does Tadado have an Imposter mode?
faq.a: No. Tadado has two modes: Forbidden Words (Taboo-style) and Heads Up. It is a fast guessing game rather than a hidden-role game, so it pairs well with Imposter on the same night.

faq.q: Which is better for big groups?
faq.a: Both work with one phone. Imposter rounds get longer as the group grows, while Tadado splits big groups into teams so everyone keeps playing every round.

faq.q: Is Tadado free like most Imposter apps?
faq.a: Tadado is free to download with the free Tadado Mix deck, no ads and no subscription. Extra themed decks and AI packs are optional one-time purchases.

tagline: The clever board game of one-word clues vs instant word guessing on one phone.
metaTitle: Codenames vs Tadado: Board Game Classic or Phone Party Game?
metaDescription: Codenames is a modern classic. Tadado is a phone party game with Forbidden Words, Heads Up, AI decks and no setup. Compare them honestly before game night.
hook: Codenames makes you think. Tadado makes you shout. If your table has both kinds of players, this comparison is for you.
about: Codenames is a team word game where two spymasters give one-word clues that link several cards on a grid of 25 words. Teammates guess which cards belong to their side while avoiding the assassin card.
It rewards clever, careful thinking and works beautifully at a table with the box laid out. The flip side is setup time and long pauses while a spymaster thinks of the perfect clue.
pickThem: Your group loves puzzles and clever wordplay
You have a table, the box and time to set up
pickTadado: You want to start in seconds, anywhere, with one phone
You want fast rounds with constant guessing and laughing
You want decks on any topic, including your own inside jokes
steps: Split into two teams, just like Codenames.
Choose Forbidden Words and pick a deck such as Genius Only for a brain-teasing challenge.
Race the timer and let Tadado keep score so nobody argues.

faq.a: No. Tadado is an independent party word game. It shares the team spirit of Codenames, but each turn you describe a single word without saying its forbidden clues.
Tadado, because it lives on your phone and works offline once downloaded. Codenames needs the box and space to lay out the cards.

faq.q: Can we play both on the same night?
faq.a: Of course. Many groups start with fast Tadado rounds to warm up, then switch to a slower strategy game later.

tagline: The pen-and-paper categories game vs a loud, fast guessing game.
metaTitle: Scattergories vs Tadado: The Better Word Game for Your Group?
metaDescription: Scattergories and Stop-style categories games are quiet writing races. Tadado is a loud guessing game with timers, scoring and AI decks. Compare them here.
hook: One game is heads down with a pen. The other is heads up with a phone on your forehead. Here is which one fits your crowd.
about: Scattergories, and the Stop or categories games it is based on, give everyone a letter and a list of categories. Players race to write an answer for each one, then compare lists and score the unique answers.
It is great for word lovers and a quiet table. Because everyone writes alone, the laughing mostly happens at the end of a round when answers get read out and challenged.
pickThem: You enjoy writing races and checking answers together
You have pens, paper and a calm table
Your group likes debating whether an answer counts
pickTadado: You want the whole group talking, acting and guessing out loud
You do not want to hunt for pens or check score sheets
You want themed and AI decks instead of the same categories

rows.feature: Timer and scoring handled for you

steps: Download Tadado and open Tadado Mix for free.
Play Forbidden Words in two teams for a fast, loud word challenge.
Missing your favorite categories? Ask the AI deck builder for a deck on any topic.

faq.a: Both are word games, but they play very differently. Scattergories is a writing race, while Tadado is a spoken guessing game with Forbidden Words and Heads Up.

faq.q: Which is better for kids and family?
faq.a: Both work. Tadado has no reading-and-writing race, so younger players can join by acting and guessing.

faq.q: Do we need anything besides a phone?
faq.a: No. Tadado handles the timer, cards and score on one phone.

tagline: Drawing to guess vs describing and acting to guess.
metaTitle: Pictionary vs Tadado: Drawing Game or Word Guessing Game?
metaDescription: Pictionary needs a pen and some drawing nerve. Tadado needs one phone and a loud voice. Compare the two party games for your next game night.
hook: Bad at drawing? Good news: in Tadado nobody needs to draw a horse. Here is how the two classics compare.
about: Pictionary is the classic drawing game: one player sketches a word while their team guesses before the timer ends. Online drawing games such as Gartic Phone have made the format popular again on phones and laptops.
Drawing games are wonderfully chaotic, but they need pens, paper or a screen to draw on, and some players freeze when it is their turn to sketch.
pickThem: Your group has budding artists and loves sketch chaos
You have a whiteboard, paper or a drawing app ready
You want quieter turns where only one person draws
pickTadado: You want nobody to feel put on the spot about drawing
You want to play anywhere, with no pens or extra screens
You want faster turns and more words per round

rows.feature: Needs pens, paper or a drawing screen

steps: Open the free Tadado Mix deck.
Choose Heads Up for an acting-style round that feels like Pictionary without the pen.
Switch to Forbidden Words when the group wants to talk instead of act.

faq.a: No. Tadado focuses on describing (Forbidden Words) and Heads Up guessing. You can still act out clues in Heads Up rounds.

faq.q: Which works better on a video call?
faq.a: Online drawing games are built for that. Tadado is designed for friends in the same room sharing one phone.

faq.q: Is Tadado good for people who hate drawing?
faq.a: Yes. That is one of the most common reasons groups switch: everyone can play without feeling judged on their art.

tagline: The salad bowl word game with paper slips vs ready-made decks on one phone.
metaTitle: Fishbowl (Salad Bowl) Game vs Tadado: Skip the Paper Slips
metaDescription: Fishbowl, Salad Bowl and Time's Up are party favorites. See how they compare with Tadado's Forbidden Words and Heads Up modes, timers and decks.
hook: Love Fishbowl but hate writing 60 paper slips? Tadado keeps the chaos and skips the prep.
about: Fishbowl, also known as Salad Bowl, Monikers or Time's Up, starts with every player writing words on slips of paper. Teams then go through the same slips over several rounds: describe freely, then use one word, then act it out.
The repeated words turn into running jokes, which is why people love it. The cost is prep time, a bowl, a timer and someone keeping score.
pickThem: You love running jokes from the same words across rounds
Your group enjoys writing its own words before playing
You have time to prep slips and a bowl
pickTadado: You want to start right now without writing anything
You want fresh words every round from themed decks
You still want custom words, made in seconds with AI
steps: Make two teams like you would for Fishbowl.
Play a Forbidden Words round, then a Heads Up round for the acting part.
Want your own words? Create an AI deck about your friends, a trip or a TV show.

faq.q: Is Tadado the same as Fishbowl?
faq.a: Not exactly. Fishbowl reuses your own paper slips across rounds. Tadado gives you ready-made or AI decks with Forbidden Words and Heads Up modes.

faq.q: Can we still play with our own words?
faq.a: Yes, through the AI deck builder: describe a topic and Tadado creates a playable deck in seconds.

faq.q: Is it good for large parties?
faq.a: Yes. Split into teams and pass the phone at the end of each turn.

tagline: Hidden roles and night phases vs a game where nobody sits out.
metaTitle: Werewolf and Mafia vs Tadado: Which Party Game Fits Your Group?
metaDescription: Werewolf and Mafia are legendary hidden-role games. Tadado is a fast word guessing game where nobody gets eliminated. Compare them for your next party.
hook: In Werewolf, eliminated players wait. In Tadado, everyone stays in until the last round. Here is when to pick each.
about: Werewolf, also played as Mafia, is a social deduction game. A moderator hands out secret roles, the werewolves pick a victim each night, and the village debates by day to find them.
It creates unforgettable drama in big groups. It also needs a moderator, works best with many players and leaves eliminated players watching for the rest of the round.
pickThem: You have a big group and someone happy to moderate
Your friends love accusations, alliances and plot twists
You have time for long, story-driven rounds
pickTadado: You want everyone playing every round, with nobody knocked out
You want to start without a moderator or role cards
You have a small group, or a mix of shy and loud players
steps: Download Tadado and open Tadado Mix.
Split into teams and play Forbidden Words as a fast warm-up.
Save Werewolf for later in the night when the group is ready for a long round.

faq.a: No. Tadado is a word guessing game with Forbidden Words and Heads Up modes. It is a different kind of fun from Werewolf, and the two work well together.
Tadado. Werewolf usually needs a bigger group to work well, while Tadado is fun with a handful of friends.

faq.q: Do we need a game master in Tadado?
faq.a: No. Tadado runs the timer, cards and score itself.
